summary: Reversed the ega.drv planar-writer transform end-to-end and resolved the redraw architecture. (A — STATIC) The maze blit is ega.drv dispatch entry 10 = FUN_1c94 (file 0x1c94). Its core is a 4-plane EGA planar read-modify-write writer (file 0x1f6e..0x20fb): per source-texture column it does `ah=src plane byte; shr ax,cl (sub-byte X align); and ax,bx (valid-pixel set-mask, built by `rcr` from cx=column-phase); merge dst=(dst & dx_clearmask)|(src & set-mask)`, writing a WORD to the off-screen page at es:[di + 0x2000*plane] (plane stride 0x2000) OR straight to A000 VRAM via the EGA Sequencer Map Mask (out 0x3c5) + Graphics Controller (0x3cf) latched read/write when [bp+0x18]&1. Outer loop (file 0x1df0..0x1f6e + the prologue clip at 0x1d7a): per-row clip against [bp+0xe](top)/[bp+0x12]/[bp+0x14], strip init/edge-mask from sub-byte X (cx=[bp-6]&7; setmask 0xff<<cl), inner-cell di stride 0x28 (=40 = one 320px row), cell-row di stride 0x140 (=320). 4 planes unrolled. (B — LIVE) The corridor REDRAW does NOT recompose the whole frame; it runs TWO stages from a transient relocated copy at runtime segment cs=0x6b91: (1) a MASKED PLANAR COMPOSITOR (the file-0x1f6e writer, transient at lin 0x6d9dd) that reads SOURCE texture seg ds=0x6a0f and writes the OFF-SCREEN PAGE es=0x4182 (di range 0x859..0x1376 = the dynamic wall columns only; the per-column `shr ax,cl` here IS the perspective convergence); then (2) a PAGE->VRAM BLIT (the cs=0x6b91 fn at ip 0x8b3, plane copies at ip 0x909/0x921/0x939/0x951) that rep-movsb-copies the page (ds=0x4182, plane src = off + p*0x2000) to A000 VRAM via the Sequencer Map Mask, OFFSET-PRESERVING WITHIN EACH CALL (si==di). The OFF-SCREEN PAGE is a 4-plane EGA image, plane p at pageBase + p*0x2000, ROW STRIDE 0x28 (40 bytes = 320px). VALIDATED: decoding the page at 40B/row 4-plane and pixel-comparing to the live framebuffer gives 99.64% on the bottom UI chrome (rows 144-199) — i.e. the page format + the page->VRAM transform + the EGA palette mapping are all CORRECT. findings.claim: The ega.drv planar writer (FUN_1c94 body, file 0x1f6e..0x20fb) is a 4-plane EGA planar read-modify-write. Per source column: `mov ah,[si+8*p]; shr ax,cl; and ax,bx; xchg al,ah; mov [bp-0xa],ax; mov ax,es:[di+0x2000*p]; and ax,dx; or ax,[bp-0xa]` then store WORD to es:[di+0x2000*p] (off-screen page) OR to A000 via Sequencer Map Mask (out 0x3c5, plane bit 1/2/4/8) + GC index (out 0x3cf) + latched `mov al,es:[di]; mov es:[di],al; mov al,es:[di+1]; mov es:[di+1],ah` when [bp+0x18]&1. The SET-MASK bx is built per column-phase at file 0x1f6b..0x1f82: `mov cx,[bp-6]; mov bh,[si]&[si+8]&[si+0x10]&[si+0x18] (transparency=AND of 4 planes); mov bl,0xff; stc; rcr bx,cl; mov dx,bx; not bx; xchg dl,dh` — so dx = clear-mask, bx = set-mask, both rotated by the sub-byte X phase (cl). The `shr ax,cl` is THE per-column horizontal sub-byte shift = the affine column placement (the perspective/convergence).

evidence.details: Capstone of ega.drv 0x1f6e..0x20c3: `mov cx,[bp-6]; mov bh,[si]; and bh,[si+8]; and bh,[si+0x10]; and bh,[si+0x18]; mov bl,0xff; stc; rcr bx,cl; mov dx,bx; not bx; xchg dl,dh; mov ah,[si]; shr ax,cl; and ax,bx; xchg al,ah; mov [bp-0xa],ax; mov ax,es:[di]; and ax,dx; or ax,[bp-0xa]; <test [bp+0x18],1; je +; VRAM seq-mask path; +> mov es:[di],ax` repeated for planes at [si+8],[si+0x10],[si+0x18] with dest es:[di+0x2000/0x4000/0x6000]. Then `inc si; add di,0x28; loop`; `add si,0x18; inc [bp-0xc]; mov di,[bp-0xc]; loop`; `pop di; add di,0x140; loop`. So inner-cell di stride 0x28 (40=1 row), cell-row di stride 0x140 (320). The byte signature `8a 3c 22 7c 08 22 7c 10 22 7c 18 b3 ff f9 d3 db` is unique in ega.drv at file 0x1f6e.

findings.claim: FUN_1c94 (file 0x1c94) bp-frame args (near-cdecl): [bp+0xa]=tile/page index (*2 into cs:[0x17a] table for the source far-seg), [bp+0xc]=clip low, [bp+0xe]=top Y, [bp+0x10]=dest-row base (*0x28 -> di), [bp+0x12]=clip cmp, [bp+0x14]=bottom Y, [bp+0x16]=flags (bit0 H-flip, bit1 V-flip + palette-remap branch), [bp+0x18]=VRAM flag (bit0 -> write A000 directly), [bp+0x1a]=piece-index-string ptr. Locals: [bp-2]=width(cells), [bp-4]=height(rows), [bp-6]=sub-byte X phase / loop counter, [bp-8]=row stride ((w-1)<<5), [bp-0xa]=di base/scratch, [bp-0xc]=di col base, [bp-0x10]=flip offset. The function clears a 0x1400-byte buffer to 0xff (transparent), reads (w,h) from a 0x18-stride descriptor at (pieceString[0]-1)*0x18, loops the piece string calling FUN_210c (0x210c) per piece, applies palette-remap (LUT @+0x192) / H-flip / V-flip, then the planar writer.

evidence.details: Ghidra FUN_0000_1c94 + capstone of the prologue 0x1c94..0x1d00: `push bp; mov bp,sp; sub sp,0x10; push ds/es/si/di; <clear 0x1400 to 0xff>; ax=[bp+0xc]<<1; bx=0x17a+ax; ds=cs:[0x169]+cs:[bx]; si=[bp+0x1a]; al=es:[si]; dec al; mul 0x18; w=[bx+2]; h=[bx+3]; <loop pieces: call 0x210c>`. findings.claim: The PAGE->VRAM blit fn (cs=0x6b91 ip 0x8b3, a transient copy) reads a 4-byte per-call descriptor at ds:[bp+0xc]: desc[0]=width-in-bytes (rep-movsb cx), desc[1]<<3 = row count ([bp-4]), desc[3]*0x140 + desc[2] = a dest base [bp-6] (desc[3] scaled by 0x140=320, desc[2]=x byte). Per row it copies `cx` bytes for each of the 4 planes (si=[bp-6]; di=si; si+=0x2000*planeIdx; out 0x3c4/2,planebit; rep movsb es:[di]<-ds:[si]) then [bp-6]+=0x28 (next row). So the blit copies a rectangle of the page to VRAM. desc[3]*0x140 vs the +0x28 row step is the SLOT-REPOSITIONING math (the descriptor places each viewport slot's page rectangle at its screen position).
